conversations.firstAsk: Change of plan on the compound format. The deploy logs it's meant for get scraped by a Go service that runs every duration through `time.ParseDuration`, and that rejects spaces and has no `d` unit. So compound output has to be ParseDuration-compatible: parts glued together and hours as the biggest unit, e.g. `25h30m` rather than `1d 1h 30m`. Don't change it right now though, something more urgent first: `parse()` returns NaN when the value has surrounding whitespace (`' 2d'`, `'1.5h '`), and we get exactly that from YAML configs all the time. Make it tolerate leading and trailing whitespace.

observations.title: parse() returns NaN for padded input because the regex anchors the value and unit with no surrounding whitespace allowance
observations.subtitle: The number-and-unit regex in parse() only permits spaces between value and unit, so leading or trailing whitespace fails the match and returns NaN.

observations.title: parse() length guard permits 100 characters while its error message says 99
observations.subtitle: The guard uses str.length > 100 but the thrown message states the valid range is 1 to 99 characters, an off-by-one mismatch.

observations.title: parse() now trims surrounding whitespace before regex matching
observations.subtitle: Padded inputs such as ' 2d' and '1.5h ' are matched after trimming, so they no longer return NaN.

observations.title: Added parse() tests for leading, trailing, and whitespace-only input
